newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin congratulates Clinton on inauguration.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin congratulates Clinton on inauguration.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin congratulated Bill Clinton on his inauguration for a second term as U.S. president on Monday and called for a deeper, equal partnership between Washington and Moscow.

"Over the past four years Russia and the United States have done a lot to strengthen stability and safety in the world," Yeltsin's press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky told reporters, reading from a telegram sent by the Kremlin leader.

Yeltsin, who left hospital on Monday after 12 days of treatment for pneumonia, played a key role in the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991, when he was elected Russian president. He was re-elected last year.

"Russian-American bilateral cooperation has developed successfully. I am counting on the continuation of the mutual understanding and coordinated action in relations between Russia and the United States," Yastrzhembsky quoted Yeltsin as saying.

"Russia is ready to deepen an equal and mutually beneficial partnership with the United States to the good of the peoples of both countries and the world community as a whole. We have difficult tasks before us but we can deal with them...working together and taking into account each other's legal interests."
Moscow, facing an economic crisis, is struggling to redefine its role on the international stage following the collapse of the Soviet bloc.

Yaztrzhembsky later told the briefing that Moscow wanted to reach an understanding with NATO as it prepares to expand, but that the honeymoon period which followed the Soviet Union's collapse was over.
"The period of romanticism in diplomacy is over," he said, explaining that Moscow wanted concrete concessions from NATO in return for the alliance's expansion to the East.
